text:
ana: Hey team — I joined yesterday but can't find the GitHub org invite in my email or on my account. Checked spam. Any tips? @it-helpdesk

it-helpdesk: Hi Ana! We sent an invite to ana+redwood@gmail.com yesterday afternoon. GitHub hides org access until you enable 2FA on your account sometimes. Do you have 2FA enabled?

ana: I don't have 2FA set up yet. I thought invites would still show. Is 2FA required for Redwood org membership?

aj: Yes, Redwood requires 2FA for org members. Quick steps: Settings → Security → Two-factor authentication. Recommended: use an authenticator app. Link: https://github.com/settings/security

it-helpdesk: After you enable 2FA, reply here and we'll resend the invite. Also reply with your GitHub username (not email) so we can add you to the right teams.

ana: OK setting it up now. Username is anagonzalez.

sam: fwiw, use an authenticator (Authy/1Password/Google) not SMS if possible. Less flaky. :lock:

devops-bot: Invite resent to anagonzalez at 1711704400. Pending team assignments: eng-runtime (write), eng-oncall (read).

ana: I accepted the invite but I don't see access to the runtime-infra repo — I can view some repos but runtime-infra is missing for me.

aj: Thanks for the heads-up. @miriam manages runtime team membership, tagging her to add you to runtime-maintainers for repo write perms.

miriam: Added anagonzalez to runtime-maintainers (gave write access to runtime-infra). You might need to refresh the org page or log out/in.

ana: Confirmed — can see runtime-infra and pushed a test branch. All good now, thanks everyone! :party_parrot:

it-helpdesk: Awesome — closing the loop. If you hit permission errors on CI or GH Actions, open a ticket with us and we'll check org-level OAuth/scopes.

ana: Will do. Appreciate the quick help!
